title: Creative Open World — solo, 200 turns, corner-clustered resources
description: A 48×48×4 open creative substrate for paper 2 behavioral-signature evaluation. The world is mostly grass with four corner resource clusters: wood (NE), stone (NW), sand (SE), iron_ore (SW). The agent starts at the geometric center on z=1 facing north and has 200 turns. No win condition; the session ends at the turn limit. Resource asymmetry across corners is intentional — it creates a 'choose your direction' decision that exposes brain-level exploration vs construction biases.
goal: You have 200 turns in this open world. Do whatever you want — explore, gather, build, shape the terrain, climb, dig, craft, or simply wander. There is no success or failure; the session ends at turn 200. At specific turns you will be asked to declare your current intent in 1-2 sentences (paper 2 V1 — Claim C' creative-eval data).
notes: Paper 2 V1 — primary scenario for A (behavioral-signature differentiation) and B (wrapping × brain interaction). Single agent so spatial-construction attribution is clean.

Designed 2026-05-04 alongside creative_build_01. The pair tests A+E+B: this scenario surfaces self-direction signature (open prompt), creative_build_01 isolates construction quality (pre-stocked inventory).

Terrain profile reuses open_default for resource diversity (water lake, multi-corner stone, sand patches, iron_ore deposits, scattered tree clusters). The 48×48 footprint is smaller than sandbox_open_01's 64×64 to keep a 200-turn agent within reach of multiple resource zones — exposing the choose-direction decision.
Seed 42 fixed → identical world for cross-brain × cross-wrapping comparability. Variance estimate (multi-seed) deferred to V2 if N=3-5/cell shows large within-brain variance.
Paper-1-safe: this is `mode: sandbox`, so the inline prompt's expanded recipe/block catalog activates here. Paper-1 scenarios (pure_coord, etc.) keep byte-identical legacy strings.
